Details

Before and after you paste

Everything the install line does, and how to undo it.

Is it safe to paste a line from the internet?

It is a fair question, so read the script first. It is one file: install.ps1. What it does:

  1. For each application, it downloads the application's published manifest and its own installer, and refuses the installer unless its SHA-256 matches the one the manifest records.
  2. That installer downloads the application from its GitHub release, and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches too. Nothing is written to your disk until every download has checked out.
{{SOURCE}}
What it changes on your computer

Everything is per user, and everything is undone by uninstalling:

    {{CHANGES}}

The window that opens has a box for each of these. To start them unticked, or to leave them out when the installer runs without a window, set any of these in the same PowerShell window before the install line:

$env:INSTALL_NO_SHORTCUTS = '1'
$env:INSTALL_NO_PATH = '1'
$env:INSTALL_NO_ASSOCIATIONS = '1'
Install only some of them

Untick the others in the window that opens. To choose ahead of it, or without a window, set INSTALL_ONLY in the same PowerShell window before the install line:

$env:INSTALL_ONLY = '{{EXAMPLE_IDS}}'

The ids are {{ID_LIST}}.

{{OPTIONAL}}
Install everything, without being asked

Run the script as a script block, which takes arguments, as the install line cannot:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm {{INSTALL_URL}}))) --install-everything --do-not-prompt-me

--install-everything installs every application, the optional ones too ($env:INSTALL_EVERYTHING = '1' does the same), and --do-not-prompt-me opens no window and asks nothing (as $env:INSTALL_QUIET = '1'). Either one works alone.

Update

Run the install line again. Each application is updated to its latest version, and one that is already current is left alone. To reinstall anyway, set $env:INSTALL_FORCE = '1' first.

Uninstall

Use Settings › Apps › Installed apps, where each application has its own entry. Or, from PowerShell, list what is installed and remove all of it:

& "{{PS_EXAMPLE_DIR}}\uninstall.cmd" -List
& "{{PS_EXAMPLE_DIR}}\uninstall.cmd" -All

The uninstaller removes exactly what was installed: files, shortcuts, PATH entries, file types and the Settings entries. Files you put in those folders yourself are left alone.
